accepted.diagnosis: Six independent, lock-verified Astro train partitions completed with exact evidence, but their rewards range from 0.587002 to 1.0 and the aggregate Recall@10 is 0.861111. A development-only replay over those task-local qrels found that lexicon-bounded English inflection variants, weighted below the preserved original terms, improve six questions without regressing any of the 24 development questions or any four-question partition.

The candidate changes the deterministic natural-query parser surface for every cited development partition while preserving explicit syntax and native Tantivy BM25. A new engine identifier is required so receipts cannot conflate the candidate with the retained baseline.

All cited traces expose query normalization in the response contract. The candidate must name its lexicon-bounded morphology policy so downstream audits can distinguish it from plain unigram normalization.

The query mutation is a durable workflow behavior supported by six distinct task checksums. The packaged skill must state that original natural terms remain dominant and that only persisted unigram variants are added.

accepted.content:
When the input contains no quoted phrase, field selector, grouping, or
uppercase Boolean operator, the consultant case-folds ASCII alphanumeric terms
and keeps only terms present in the validated persisted classical unigram
lexicon. Each retained original receives weight `3.0`. Deterministic `s`, `es`,
`ies`, `ing`, and `ed` transformations may add at most two variants that also
exist in that immutable unigram lexicon, each at weight `0.35`. This bounded
expansion handles common English inflections without external synonyms, qrels,
or corpus mutation. Any explicit Tantivy syntax is preserved byte-for-byte.
Inspect `parsed_query` and `engine.query_normalization` to verify the choice.
